caption: This drawing features two three-dimensional, carved wooden stamps positioned toward the center, rendered in natural brown tones with blue-gray details accentuating their patterns. Surrounding these stamps on all sides are a series of black line drawings depicting a variety of intricate embroidery patterns, each arranged symmetrically to create a balanced composition. The designs are floral, geometric, and foliate, with some composed of repeated leafy or curving motifs and others of loops, dots, or abstract shapes. The background is a light beige, and the upper part of the drawing contains the printed gray text “EARLY AMERICAN EMBROIDERY STAMPS.” At the bottom right, the name “CHARLOTTE ANGUS” is printed in smaller gray text.
title: Stamps for Embroidery
